Both the valid prefix and the error region causally drive the reflection gain, whereas removing these components (Shuffled GNT, Answer Only) reduces accuracy below the direct baseline.

top_papers.title: Should We Type or Talk to LLM Agents? A Comprehensive Study of Voice and Keyboard Input Perturbations
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates how voice and keyboard input affect Large Language Model (LLM) performance. The authors introduce HIVE, a tool to simulate real-world input variations, and find that voice transcription errors, particularly structural changes, significantly degrade LLM accuracy. Keyboard input perturbations are less impactful, with both input types' performance degradation stemming from the loss of original query tokens.
top_papers.figure_caption: The HIVE taxonomy at a glance. A user either ad-libs a question or passes existing information along, and it reaches the model through voice, a QWERTY keyboard, or copy-paste, which delivers the question verbatim and is the clean reference. Colour marks the channel, not how an operator is built: the voice operators are a mix of few-shot LLM style transfer and deterministic rules, and the keyboard operators are all deterministic. Every example shown is a real item from the released data. The right panel shows how a model replies under degraded input. Table 4 gives the full specification.

top_papers.title: Socially Grounded Agentic AI: Coordinating Plural Perspectives through Social Theory
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes "Socially Grounded Agentic AI" to address pluralistic alignment by leveraging social theory. It argues that AI systems need to represent and coordinate multiple legitimate perspectives, moving beyond single-value optimization. The core method involves using sociological concepts like roles, interaction, and power dynamics to inform AI design for better handling diverse social contexts.

top_papers.title: Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning LLMs: Inference Regimes, Evaluation, and Reproducibility
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a systematic framework to understand and compare different "test-time scaling" methods for LLMs. It formalizes these methods as budgeted inference over an implicit prefix tree, categorizing them into three structural regimes. This work's contribution is to provide a unified account that addresses the current lack of comparability in research due to diverse inference protocols.
top_papers.figure_caption: A selective chronicle of reasoning systems, from elicited chains to budgeted inference. Test-time inference expanded from single-trajectory elicitation and leaf-level sampling with terminal reduction to include prefix-level search and budget-aware control ( Section ˜ 2.1 ), while model and interface mechanisms evolved through verified distillation, reward optimization, explicit reasoning controls, and parameter-space composition (Appendices D and E ). The lower bands summarize the evaluation and reproducibility requirements developed in Section ˜ 3 and the evaluated object used throughout this paper: checkpoint, prompt, decoder, controller or reducer, verifier or judge, budget, and stopping rule, with utility, candidate-bank profile, cost, and uncertainty reported together. Green dots mark families represented in the experimental roster; dashed boxes denote contextual milestones. Era labels indicate shifts in emphasis rather than mutually exclusive periods.

top_papers.title: The Transformer Revolution, Part 1: Dynamic Processing through Output- Weight Interconnections
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a new interpretation of Transformer inference, arguing that they perform dynamic, prompt-dependent transformations rather than simply reproducing training data. The core method, Sequence-level Interactive Dynamic Parallel Processing (SIDPP), views Transformers as systems that transform concepts (token vectors) using other concepts (parameterized transformations, which can be dynamic). The key contribution is identifying how output-weight interconnections, where outputs influence weights, enable this dynamic computation.

top_papers.title: Video-DeepResearch: Towards the Next-Generation Multimodal Deepresearch Agent
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Video-DeepResearch (Video-DR), a multimodal agent designed for open-web exploration of video streams. Its core method involves a decoupled perception-exploration pipeline that prioritizes dense spatiotemporal visual grounding before web retrieval, addressing modality bias and parametric knowledge leakage. The contribution lies in this novel framework and its two-stage training, enabling autonomous exploration beyond imitation learning, and a new benchmark for evaluating such agents.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of the Video-DeepResearch pipeline.

top_papers.title: HalluTruthQA-4K: A Fine-Grained Corpus and Annotation Process for Arabic Hallucination Detection and Truth Verification
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces HalluTruthQA-4K, a detailed Arabic dataset for detecting and verifying factual errors in language model responses. Its core method involves expert curation of 4,000 question-answering instances with character-level annotations of hallucinations, providing more granular insights than previous binary labels. The contribution lies in offering a richer resource to improve Arabic hallucination detection and truth verification.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of the HalluTruthQA-4K construction and annotation pipeline. Questions and reference answers are prepared and verified by domain experts, free-form answers are generated using Fanar-1-9B-Instruct , and the resulting instances undergo expert annotation followed by an independent verification pass.

top_papers.title: ParVL: Parallel Scaling and Expandable Compute Allocation for Multimodal LLMs
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces ParVL, a framework for scaling Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) by reusing existing backbone parameters across parallel vision and language branches.  Instead of increasing model size or sequential inference, ParVL reallocates computation to optimize task-specific performance. Its core contribution is a novel parallel scaling strategy that addresses the rigid computation allocation in existing MLLMs.
top_papers.figure_caption: Fixed vs. expandable compute allocation in MLLMs. (Left) Existing multimodal models suffer from a fixed compute allocation between ViT (vision) and LLM (language) components during the SFT phase, which is visualized as a locked seesaw. (Right) Our ParVL framework enables expandable and flexible compute for the two modules. By leveraging extensive parameter reuse, our parallel architecture independently scales computation in the vision and language modules during SFT, enabling controlled comparison of different vision–language allocations across branch-count configurations.

top_papers.title: PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents
top_papers.abstract: PAST-Bench is a new benchmark designed to systematically evaluate whether personal AI agents improve over time by effectively utilizing their retained experience. The core method involves running agents through task sequences with and without access to their past experiences, under matched conditions. The paper's contribution is demonstrating that while recursive self-improvement is real in these agents, its effectiveness varies significantly across different capabilities and agent frameworks, and often lacks clear evidence of proper experience utilization.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of PAST-Bench . The benchmark tests whether agents improve across sessions by reusing retained experience, covering four capability dimensions, 26 task-family scenarios, and 204 episode tasks with matched no-persistence controls.

top_papers.title: SocietyBench: Forecasting Counterfactual Social-World Evolution
top_papers.abstract: SocietyBench introduces a novel benchmark for evaluating LLMs' ability to forecast social-world evolution. Its core method involves creating counterfactual timelines of real-world events by anonymizing entities and shifting dates, then posing forecasting questions about future developments. The contribution lies in providing a structured way to measure LLMs' understanding of social dynamics and temporal accuracy, moving beyond task completion to assess predictive social intelligence.
top_papers.figure_caption: Why SocietyBench evaluates counterfactual forecasting rather than event recall. Evaluated on a real, widely reported event in its original form, a model can score well simply by recognizing the event from pre-training data. SocietyBench replaces the entities and shifts the dates while preserving the causal and temporal structure, so the model has to forecast the future of an arc it cannot recognize.

top_papers.title: WorldCup Arena: Prospective, Leakage-Free Evaluation of Frontier LLMs on a Live Tournament
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces WorldCup Arena, a novel method for evaluating Large Language Models' (LLMs) forecasting abilities in real-time, preventing data leakage by querying models before events occur. The study tracked six frontier LLMs' predictions for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, revealing that their accuracy on match outcomes, while competitive, largely mirrors betting on favorites, and they exhibit high agreement with each other.
top_papers.figure_caption: Top: a retrospective evaluation asks after the event resolves; this study asks before kickoff. Bottom: the pipeline at one fixture, from the frozen pre-match package to the settled result.

top_papers.title: ABSeeker: Training Long-Horizon Search Agents via Answer-Backtracked Credit Assignment
top_papers.abstract: ABSeeker trains long-horizon search agents by assigning credit at a granular, step-by-step level rather than just at the trajectory's end. Its core method, Answer-Backtracked Credit Assignment (ABC), recovers intermediate clues from the ground-truth answer to create dense supervision, rewarding helpful actions and penalizing unhelpful ones throughout the search process. This approach improves agent performance by providing more informative feedback during training.
top_papers.figure_caption: ABSeeker achieves the best performance among 4B models and remains competitive with several larger search agents. Striped regions indicate results with context management enabled.

top_papers.title: CoPlan: A Trustworthy Co-Intelligence Interface for Care Planning through Role-Based Contestable Argument Graphs
top_papers.abstract: CoPlan is a co-intelligent interface for care planning that uses specialized AI agents to generate candidate interventions and supporting or challenging arguments. Its core method involves a multi-agent workflow where human care planners can inspect, revise, and justify AI recommendations, fostering trust and collaboration. The main contribution is a contestable interface that allows for human-AI co-intelligence, ensuring plans align with clinical judgment and patient values.
top_papers.figure_caption: Human-AI Co-Intelligence Mechanism through Contestability for Agentic AI in Care Planning Systems.

top_papers.title: Gradient Immunity: Null-Space Resistance to Malicious Fine-Tuning
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces "Gradient Immunity" to defend against malicious fine-tuning of open-weight language models. The core method is the Unidirectional Safety Gate (USG), which uses a cubic layer to block harmful gradients and an inverse adapter to preserve normal model behavior. This approach protects models in a partially protected open-weight release setting, where most weights are trainable but a safety component is preserved.
top_papers.figure_caption: The figure illustrates the idealized behavior of a USG-style safeguard. For harmful data, it functions as a diode: during backpropagation, the USG sets gradients to zero, inducing gradient vanishing and thereby blocking gradient propagation. For safe data, it acts as a wire without inducing gradient vanishing in the idealized exact-blocking definition. Its core idea is the controllable induction of gradient vanishing—normally an undesirable behavior in model training.

top_papers.title: OPD-V: Visual On-Policy Self-Distillation with Modality Balance
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces OPD-V, a novel visual on-policy self-distillation method for multimodal large language models (MLLMs). It addresses the issue of modality imbalance, where text often dominates over visual information during reasoning. OPD-V leverages the concept of modality balance itself as privileged information, using a "Positive Teacher" (Zoom-In Image) to guide distillation and improve the model's ability to integrate diverse visual inputs.
top_papers.figure_caption: Modality Balance as privileged information, evaluated on 5K samples drawn from multiple domains. Left: the Modality-Balance Attention Ratio is lowest for the Negative Teacher with the Mask Image, intermediate for the student with the Original Image, and highest for the Positive Teacher with the Zoom-In Image. These matched conditions expose distinct degrees of Modality Imbalance. Right: as the Modality-Balance Logits Margin increases, the gap between the Positive and Negative Teacher attention ratios widens, accompanied by higher student correctness. For each margin interval b b , the blue curve reports Δ ​ ρ b = | b | − 1 ​ ∑ i ∈ b [ ρ ​ ( c + ; y i ) − ρ ​ ( c − ; y i ) ] \( \Delta \)\( \rho_{b} \)=|b|^{-1}\( \sum_{i\in b} \)[\( \rho \)(c^{+};y_{i})-\( \rho \)(c^{-};y_{i})] , where y i y_{i} is the response trajectory for sample i i , and c + c^{+} and c − c^{-} denote the Zoom-In Image and Mask Image conditions, respectively.

top_papers.title: Protoreasoning in Tiny Transformers
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces "protoreasoning," a simplified Chain of Thought method for tiny transformer models. By applying this to reasoning-friendly tasks on Dyck languages, the authors demonstrate that these small models can achieve improved out-of-distribution generalization. This approach allows for detailed analysis of step-by-step reasoning in models far smaller than typical LLMs, offering insights into how such reasoning is learned.

top_papers.title: DASyR-LLM: Domain-Aware Symbolic Regression with LLMs for Kinetic Model Discovery
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces DASyR-LLM, a novel framework for automated kinetic model discovery. It integrates a Large Language Model (LLM) into an iterative symbolic regression process. The LLM acts as a domain expert, critiquing candidate models for physical plausibility and proposing new, chemically informed rate expressions, thereby improving the accuracy and interpretability of discovered kinetic models.

top_papers.title: SparseDitto: Customizing GPU Kernels for Different Sparsity Patterns with LLM-Based Agentic System
top_papers.abstract: SparseDitto tackles the challenge of optimizing GPU sparse matrix kernels by using an LLM-based agentic system. Its core method involves analyzing input matrix sparsity patterns and target GPUs to dynamically generate customized kernels. The key contribution is a system that adapts representation, execution strategy, and hardware mapping for each specific workload, overcoming the limitations of static, one-size-fits-all implementations and achieving significant performance gains.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. One 16 × 16 16\( \times \) 16 matrix exposes intrinsic pattern cues and format-induced costs. The matrix contains an irregular dense tile, a high-degree column, an empty row, and uneven row lengths. CSR and CSC traverse compressed rows and columns, respectively. SELL-C with C = 8 C=8 introduces slice-local padding, while 4 × 4 4\( \times \) 4 BSR introduces block fill. The right column shows the resulting work granularity and imbalance for rows, columns, slice slots, and blocks.

top_papers.title: Toward Skill-Native LLMs: Skill Entropy for Benchmarking and Training Long-Horizon Reasoning
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces "Skill Entropy" to measure the difficulty of skill switching in long-horizon reasoning tasks. They propose "Skill^2-Bench," a benchmark designed to evaluate and train LLMs on these cross-skill tasks. Their findings reveal a significant "skill-switching gap" in current LLMs, where performance degrades as tasks require more complex skill transitions.
top_papers.figure_caption: Skill Entropy for Benchmarking and Training Skill-Native LLMs. We define a cross-skill long-horizon task as a sequence of question steps that each invoke a different reasoning skill, and skill entropy as a quantity measuring the difficulty of switching from one skill to another. We present: (1) Skill 2 -Bench : a benchmark over 558 558 skills across 9 9 verifiable and open-ended domains. Each task is graded by a task-level skill entropy; frontier models degrade nearly monotonically as task-level skill entropy increases. (2) Skill-Entropy RL: an RL framework where the model predicts not only the answer at each step but also the skill used to produce it. The reward combines step-level correctness with a skill-entropy reward that measures alignment between the model-predicted skill sequence and the gold skill chain. See Section ˜ 3 and Section ˜ 4 for details.

top_papers.title: Towards Physics of Multimodal Pretraining: Knowledge Flow, Modality Synergy, Early Unification, and Recipes
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates the underlying principles of multimodal pretraining by systematically exploring how different modalities interact. Its core contribution lies in empirically identifying four key "physics" of this process: knowledge flow patterns, the conditions for synergy versus competition between modalities, the benefits of early unification, and practical "recipes" for effective multimodal training.
top_papers.figure_caption: Impact of scaling language data on visual understanding and generation. Increasing the language ratio universally improves both vision capabilities.

top_papers.title: DelusionEval: Measuring Delusion-Linked Behaviors in AI Chatbots
top_papers.abstract: DelusionEval is a novel evaluation protocol designed to measure how AI chatbots might exacerbate user delusions. It uses real-world conversation histories from individuals who experienced psychological harm to prompt LLMs and assess their tendency to engage in delusion-promoting behaviors. The study found that model size or reasoning capabilities didn't predict this tendency, but longer conversation histories significantly increased the risk.

top_papers.title: Spoken Function Calling: A New Perspective on Spoken Language Understanding for Large Audio Language Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Spoken Function Calling (SFC), a novel approach to Spoken Language Understanding (SLU) for large audio language models. SFC optimizes semantic understanding by using structured rule definitions, moving beyond the limitations of traditional closed-set SLU. The contribution lies in developing the SFC framework, creating a benchmark dataset (SFC-Bench), and demonstrating its effectiveness in enhancing the function-calling capabilities of audio language models.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Comparison of traditional SLU and proposed SFC. SFC resolves parameter ambiguity through a precise and structured function definition.

top_papers.title: Benchmarking the Benchmarks: Evaluating Benchmarks for Conversational Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel, reference-free framework that leverages LLM judges to assess the quality of conversational agent benchmarks. Its core method involves evaluating benchmark consistency, complexity, and policy coverage, providing actionable diagnostics. The key contribution is a practical approach to reliably identify and improve flawed benchmarks, ensuring more accurate evaluations of conversational agents.

top_papers.title: From Passive Mirrors to Active Agents: Holonic Digital Twins for Physical AI over Networks
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes Holonic Digital Twins (HDT-Nets) to enable real-time physical AI over networks. Unlike passive digital twins, HDTs are active agents that reason about their environment, allowing for reliable world modeling and long-horizon planning under uncertainty. This framework addresses limitations of current AI in physical systems by leveraging wireless networks for coordinated, context-aware physical intelligence.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of Proposed HDT-Net.

top_papers.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces HarnessOpt-Bench, a novel benchmark for evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) in the task of harness optimization. The core method involves an LLM-based optimizer iteratively improving a given LLM agent's surrounding code (harness) based on graded feedback and a limited evaluation budget. The main contribution is providing a standardized protocol to measure LLMs' ability to optimize their own deployment, addressing a gap in current AI system evaluation.
top_papers.figure_caption: Trusted execution for held-out harness optimization. The optimizer can write only the target agent’s harness. It can read the evaluation results and the target task data but not modify them. The optimizer receives per-case development traces and aggregate validation metrics, while test cases and scores remain inaccessible behind the trusted evaluation server. Each candidate is evaluated in isolated, unprivileged sandboxes, and every model call, both the optimizer’s own and the evaluations’, passes through a gateway that enforces model allow-lists and per-scope budgets. The test partition is evaluated only after the optimizer nominates a final candidate. Because held-out data, provider credentials, and budget enforcement are absent from the optimizer’s sandbox, these restrictions are properties of the execution environment rather than instructions the optimizer is expected to follow.

top_papers.title: Improving the Realism of Synthetic Clinical Benchmarks Under Utility Constraints
top_papers.abstract: This paper addresses the issue of synthetic clinical benchmarks being unrealistic despite passing utility checks, particularly in privacy-sensitive healthcare. The core method is to improve benchmark realism while maintaining downstream utility, framing it as a "utility-constrained realism improvement" problem. The contribution lies in proposing and demonstrating a framework to enhance synthetic data realism through metrics like missingness structure and population alignment, ensuring practical usefulness for AI agents.

top_papers.title: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces the Nimblemind Multi-Agent System (nMAS), an automated pipeline for engineering heart failure features from electronic health records. nMAS addresses the bottleneck of manual feature engineering by integrating clinical reasoning and evidence traceability. Its core contribution is a rubric-grounded system that generates verified, aggregated features, significantly improving the performance of heart failure prediction models.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of the nMAS heart-failure feature-extraction pipeline.

top_papers.title: What Current AI Benchmarks Leave Unmeasured: Modality, Search, Citations, and Implications (for Safety Evaluations)
top_papers.abstract: This paper argues that current AI benchmarks for LLMs are insufficient for safety evaluations because they overlook crucial factors like modality, search capabilities, and citation grounding. By comparing API and chat UI access with and without web search on existing benchmarks, the authors reveal that these unmeasured dimensions significantly impact model behavior and reliability, highlighting a critical gap in current assessment practices.
top_papers.figure_caption: Average per-run accuracy across modalities and search conditions. Error bars represent 95% confidence intervals.

top_papers.title: A Six-Dimensional Taxonomy of Post-Training Adaptation Techniques with Applications in AI Governance
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a six-dimensional taxonomy to systematically categorize and understand the diverse landscape of post-training adaptation techniques in machine learning. By organizing methods based on mechanism, goal, data, persistence, scope, and model type, it clarifies distinctions between similar techniques and maps their evolution across different model architectures. This contribution provides a unified framework for analyzing and comparing adaptation strategies, crucial for AI governance and responsible model development.

top_papers.title: Benchmarking and Enhancing LLMs for Rule-Intensive Review of National Standard Documents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces GB/T-Bench, the first benchmark designed to evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) in reviewing rule-intensive national standard documents. The benchmark utilizes a hierarchical taxonomy to assess LLMs on aspects like document structure, scope, terminology, and normative consistency, identifying 25 specific error types. This work aims to improve LLM performance in professional document review, a task currently reliant on costly human expertise.
top_papers.figure_caption: A GB/T document review case and dataset statistics of GB/T-Bench.

top_papers.title: NeSy-RAG: Neuro-Symbolic RAG for Explainable Question Answering
top_papers.abstract: NeSy-RAG is a neuro-symbolic framework that enhances explainable question answering by augmenting retrieval-based methods. It converts retrieved text into attributable Prolog modules, enabling verifiable reasoning and clear evidence attribution. The system also detects and addresses missing user context by identifying crucial facts needed for accurate query resolution.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of the proposed NeSy-RAG framework

top_papers.title: RP-OPSD: Reasoning-Pivot-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multilingual Reasoning Transfer
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces RP-OPSD, a novel method for multilingual reasoning transfer in LLMs. It addresses the limitation of existing on-policy self-distillation by focusing distillation efforts on "reasoning pivots" – critical decision points in the reasoning process. RP-OPSD uses the distributional shift between teacher outputs with and without an English reference to identify and guide distillation around these pivots, improving cross-lingual reasoning capabilities.
top_papers.figure_caption: Motivation of reasoning-pivot-guided transfer. Surface variants can preserve the same reasoning state, while pivot drift corrupts downstream reasoning. RP-OPSD uses the distribution gap between the solution-conditioned view q t + q_{t}^{+} and the ablated view q t − q_{t}^{-} to identify reasoning-sensitive tokens. The Frence CoT means ”So we multiply 4 by 3, which makes 12”.

top_papers.title: The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Programmatic Tool Calling (PTC), a method that allows LLMs to invoke tools as executable Python scripts, enabling more natural chaining and parallelization than traditional JSON calls. Empirically, PTC matches or surpasses JSON tool calling across most tested models on the BFCL v4 benchmark, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential for improved agent capabilities.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of the two primary paradigms evaluated. In JSON tool calling , the model emits JSON tool-call objects via the API. In programmatic tool calling , it writes a Python script using typed stubs; the agent loop executes it in a subprocess. A filesystem-discovery condition is included as a secondary reference point.

top_papers.title: A Theory of Post-hoc Debate Judgement
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a formal theory for post-hoc debate judgment, aiming to improve the reliability and interpretability of AI debates. The core method involves identifying and testing formal properties like reproducibility and groundedness for judgment mechanisms. The contribution lies in providing a theoretical framework and empirical validation for evaluating debate outcomes, particularly for claim verification tasks.

top_papers.title: Beyond the Transcript: Detecting Covert Co ordination in Latent Multi-Agent Communication
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Verifiable Latent Alignments (VLA), a framework to detect and control covert coordination in multi-agent language models by analyzing their hidden communication states. VLA links private latent states to public actions for causal analysis, offering a novel three-layer monitor and a steerability framework. Its core contribution is enabling the detection of hidden harmful coordination and providing mechanisms to influence these private communication channels.

top_papers.title: DA-WAM: Decision-Aligned Future Latents for Driving World Models
top_papers.abstract: DA-WAM unifies future prediction and trajectory selection for autonomous driving by learning decision-informative latent representations. Its core method involves an action-conditioned world model that directly influences trajectory scoring, ensuring predicted futures guide planning. This approach's contribution is enabling world models to actively shape decision-making, rather than just providing passive predictions.
top_papers.figure_caption: Prediction–action alignment in trajectory scoring. (a) Trajectory-only prediction provides no explicit future representation to the scorer. (b) Loosely coupled latent fusion incorporates a future representation but generates only a single trajectory proposal, precluding candidate-specific future comparison. (c) Sharing one future latent across multiple candidates creates a prediction–action mismatch. (d) DA-WAM predicts a distinct future latent for each candidate and scores the trajectory with its corresponding latent, establishing a one-to-one trajectory–future correspondence.

top_papers.title: Harness Continual Learning: Continual Adaptation Beyond Model Parameters
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Harness Continual Learning (HCL), a new paradigm where an agent adapts by evolving its "harness" of prompts, memories, tools, and routing rules around a frozen foundation model, rather than just updating model parameters. The core contribution is addressing "harness-level forgetting," where changes to these external components can disrupt previously learned behaviors. HCL proposes mechanisms like guarded harness evolution to manage this adaptation and retain acquired capabilities.
top_papers.figure_caption: The shift in the object of continual learning. Model-centric methods update model parameters \( \theta \) over sequential experience. HCL instead updates harness state around a frozen foundation model. In both settings, adaptation can improve new behavior while interfering with behavior acquired earlier.

top_papers.title: SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments
top_papers.abstract: SPADE is a self-play reinforcement learning framework where a single LLM acts as both an Environment Designer and a Reasoning Agent. The Environment Designer generates diverse, long-horizon training environments as executable code, while the Reasoning Agent learns to act within them. This allows for continuous self-improvement by adaptively creating new training scenarios based on the agent's learning progress, measured by its regret.

top_papers.title: What is Missing from AI Post-Training AI: An Empirical Analysis
top_papers.abstract: This paper empirically analyzes LLM agents performing post-training tasks. It distinguishes between execution-level capability (iterating within a strategy) and strategy-level capability (revising the strategy). The authors find that current agents are largely limited to the former, spending their entire budget on local adjustments within an initial, fixed strategy. Their contribution lies in demonstrating this limitation and proposing an experience-driven scaffold to improve performance by enabling strategy revision.

top_papers.title: Grading the Graders: Verification Autonomy Levels (L0-L5) for LLM Reasoning
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Verification Autonomy Levels (VAL), a new framework to standardize how we evaluate LLM verifiers. VAL classifies verification methods based on the origin of their specifications and the guarantees they provide, ranging from LLM self-assessment (L0) to provable correctness (L3/L4). The core contribution is a unified way to understand and compare the reliability and autonomy of different LLM verification techniques.

top_papers.title: AI4AI-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Algorithmic Design for Recursive Self-Improvement
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces AI4AI-Bench, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate an AI agent's ability to design training algorithms, a key step towards recursive self-improvement (RSI). The benchmark consists of 10 frozen research repositories, where agents must rewrite training algorithms within a time limit. The contribution lies in isolating and measuring the capacity for algorithmic design, a capability not addressed by existing benchmarks.

top_papers.title: DARS: Dual-Level Credit Assignment RL with Structured Reasoning for Instruction-Based Image Editing
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces DARS, a reinforcement learning framework for instruction-based image editing. DARS addresses the inefficiency of traditional training by employing dual-level credit assignment. It uses multi-plan/multi-render rollouts to determine how to adjust the planner and renderer, and a structured reasoning output within the planner to provide localized supervision for better edit execution.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Two visually poor editing outcomes can require opposite cross-module update emphases. Case A : the planner captures the requested edit reasonably well, but the renderer fails to realize it, so this sample should place more corrective update weight on the renderer. Case B : the sampled plan is a less useful intermediate for the instruction, and the renderer faithfully executes it, so this sample should place more corrective update weight on the planner. DARS is designed to distinguish render-dominant from plan-dominant update needs through routing signals; when planner-side emphasis is needed, its structured slots support finer within-planner diagnosis. Teaser showing two low-scoring failure cases in a two-stage image editing pipeline that require opposite cross-module credit-assignment decisions: one should emphasize renderer correction, while the other should emphasize planner correction.

top_papers.title: From Agent Behaviour to Agent-Friendly Documentation: An Empirical Study of How Coding Agents Discover, Read, and Write Technical Documentation
top_papers.abstract: This study empirically investigates how coding agents interact with technical documentation. It reveals that agents primarily consult agent-facing artifacts like instruction files and working notes, rather than traditional technical documentation or API references. This finding challenges current documentation practices, suggesting a need to adapt documentation strategies for agent consumption.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Agents’ documentation interactions across 557 SWE-chat sessions (panels a–d, n = 3,033 n=3{,}033 documentation events) and 33,097 AIDev agentic pull requests (panel e). (a) Agent-facing documents — instruction files and agent working notes — account for 60.5% of interactions, whereas API references account for 1.3%; the right-hand column uses a magnified axis. (b) Testing and building are less frequent within three events of a consultation and remain so after adjustment; the two authoring outcomes differ between the unadjusted lift and the stage-adjusted odds ratio, so those associations remain unresolved. Intervals are session-level cluster-bootstrap estimates. (c) Interaction is predominantly self-initiated (70.2% of all 3,033 interactions; 62.5% of the 1,615 consultation events) rather than failure-driven (7.5%; 9.7%); the axis counts all interactions. (d) Of ten candidate stages, Validate and Escalate have zero events under our operational definitions (open markers); stages overlap and do not sum to 3,033. (e) Among pull requests that change both code and documentation, code is touched first 4.7 × \( \times \) more often, although 42.6% first touch both in a single commit, for which no order is observable; panel e uses a different dataset and unit of analysis (pull requests), and its error bars are Wilson intervals — the repository cluster-bootstrap equivalents are in Table 6 . Five panels summarising document types, post-consultation actions, interaction triggers, candidate interaction stages, and code–documentation ordering in pull requests.

top_papers.title: Inducing Task Models from Computer-Use Traces
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Task Model Induction (TMI), a method to automatically generate structured, reusable models of everyday computer tasks from passively recorded user activity. TMI addresses the challenge of multi-threaded work by discovering latent tasks and then creating a hierarchical objective model and a control flow procedure model for each. This enables agents to learn real-world workflows and organizations to audit and reuse this knowledge.
top_papers.figure_caption: Task model induction from computer-use traces. Screenshots and input events are grounded into semantic actions, whose interleaved spans are assigned to latent tasks. Each task is represented as a hierarchy pairing objectives with control-flow operators.

top_papers.title: The Third Restructuring of Software Form: From the Three-Tier Architecture to Storage, Models, and Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes Software 3.0, a new paradigm where context and reasoning drive software behavior, moving beyond instruction- or data-driven approaches. Its core method is to identify the terminal form of this shift as a convergence of a generalized database, a large model for reasoning, and an agent for execution. The contribution lies in predicting how this new form will restructure existing software architectures, with the model absorbing UI, business logic re-partitioned, and data becoming a unified abstraction.

top_papers.title: Reward-Guided Autoregressive Graph Generation for Efficient Multi-Agent Communication Topology Design
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces RGA-Designer, a method for efficiently designing communication topologies in multi-agent systems. It adapts Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) by training a reward model that balances task accuracy with topology sparsity. This approach fine-tunes an autoregressive graph generator, significantly reducing token consumption while maintaining performance.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of our reward-guided pipeline for MAS topology generation.

top_papers.title: ConceptGuard: Benchmarking Context-Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces **ConceptGuard**, a novel benchmark for evaluating context-sensitive unlearning in LLMs. Its core method focuses on **dual-use concepts**, which have both harmful and benign applications, to assess if LLMs can selectively remove unsafe knowledge while preserving beneficial uses. The main contribution is a more realistic evaluation framework that moves beyond simple factual recall to measure the conceptual understanding and control required for practical unlearning.

top_papers.title: FormalTCS: Benchmarking End-to-End Frontier Formal Theoretical Computer Science Research of Large Language Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces FormalTCS, an expert-validated benchmark for evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) on realistic, end-to-end theoretical computer science (TCS) research tasks. The benchmark features formalizations and proofs from recent top-tier TCS papers, highlighting that current LLMs struggle significantly with the autoformalization step, translating natural language into formal statements. This work aims to push LLM capabilities towards autonomously conducting TCS research.

top_papers.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration with the Common-Sense Reasoning Capabilities of LLMs for Autonomous Driving
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid framework for autonomous driving that combines reinforcement learning (RL) and PID control, orchestrated by a Large Language Model (LLM). The LLM's common-sense reasoning is used to guide the RL agent and iteratively refine its reward function, improving decision-making in complex scenarios. This approach aims to leverage LLM reasoning for contextual understanding without direct vehicle control, mitigating latency and hallucination risks.
top_papers.figure_caption: High-level system architecture.

top_papers.title: AI with Authority, from Application to Silicon
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces the "Salt method," a novel approach that leverages generative AI to make machine verification economical and essential for productivity. The core method involves using a proof kernel to ensure mathematical claims are checked between AI agents, reserving human attention for high-level decisions. This allows a single researcher to direct autonomous machine work from application code to a taped-out RISC-V processor without human RTL design or proof review, significantly accelerating development.

top_papers.title: AUSO: Action-Level Unified Skill Optimization from Internalization to Utilization
top_papers.abstract: AUSO unifies skill learning and utilization by optimizing them at the action level throughout an agent's policy evolution. This progressive approach allows the agent to first acquire foundational skills from teacher guidance and environmental feedback, and then selectively use these skills to improve individual decisions as training progresses. The core contribution is a more efficient and effective skill learning framework that avoids fragmentation and assigns appropriate importance to skill guidance at different stages of an agent's development.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Empirical evidence of ambiguous medium/easy skill-routing boundaries in Skill0.5. Samples across the success threshold can differ by as little as 1 / 8 1/8 , revealing the ambiguity of threshold-based routing.

top_papers.title: Personalized Privacy Control in LLMs via Attention Head Intervention
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces "personalized privacy" for LLMs, recognizing that acceptable data disclosure varies by user, not just context. They propose P3Bench, a benchmark for evaluating personalized privacy policies, and \textsc{Repair}, an inference-time method that intervenes in attention heads to robustly enforce these user-specific privacy preferences, overcoming the limitations of prompt-based methods.
top_papers.figure_caption: Failure of Personalized Privacy Control. LLM agents may ignore the user’s privacy policy and disclose contextually appropriate sensitive information based on their own judgment during task execution.

top_papers.title: Re$^3$Cap: Retrieval-Guided Refinement for Image Captioning Enhancement via Reinforcement Learning
top_papers.abstract: Re$^3$Cap enhances image captioning by using multi-modal retrieval as a reasoning signal to refine generated captions. It identifies and corrects hallucinations and omissions without needing extra annotations, leading to more accurate and detailed descriptions. This retrieval-guided approach surpasses previous reinforcement learning methods and even supervised fine-tuning.
top_papers.figure_caption: Reasoning strategy of Caption Refinement Suggester (CRS) and Caption Quality Assessor (CQA). We leverage k-core subgraph computation to analyze critical textual content in the retrieval results. Specifically, CRS extracts overlapping sentences S v k S^{k}_{v} from the image retrieval results and uses them as signals to guide LVLMs to incorporate these key elements into their generated descriptions. By analyzing the discrepancy between S v k S^{k}_{v} and caption-retrieved results S c k S^{k}_{c} , CQA identifies hallucinations ( S c k − S v ​ c k S^{k}_{c}-S^{k}_{vc} ) and omissions ( S v k − S v ​ c k S^{k}_{v}-S^{k}_{vc} ) in this caption.

top_papers.title: Utility Under Attack: Agent Memory Poisoning and the Limits of Content Screening and Provenance Ranking
top_papers.abstract: This paper demonstrates that agent memory poisoning, where false information is injected into an AI's persistent memory, significantly degrades its accuracy. The authors show that standard content screening and provenance ranking methods are ineffective against this attack. Their key contribution is highlighting that distinguishing true from false information often requires external grounding, beyond just the text itself.

top_papers.title: A Neurosymbolic Approach for Constructing Planning Domain Models from Clinical Narratives
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces NSPIN, a neurosymbolic framework that constructs planning domain models from unstructured clinical narratives. NSPIN uses a pre-trained LLM to extract and impute structured event sequences, then induces a PPDDL model and refines it with LLM-proposed revisions validated empirically. The core contribution is a novel method for formalizing complex surgical workflows from text, enabling better decision support by generating generalizable planning models.

top_papers.title: Asymmetric Capacity Allocation in Self-Refinement Pipelines
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates how to optimally allocate model sizes within self-refinement pipelines (generation, critique, revision). The core method involves systematically varying model sizes for each stage across multiple benchmarks. The key contribution is demonstrating that larger generators and refiners are beneficial, while the critic's size has minimal impact, suggesting resource optimization by using smaller critic models.

top_papers.title: Thermo-FL: Thermal-Aware Robust Federated Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models for Edge AI
top_papers.abstract: Thermo-FL addresses the dual challenges of hardware thermal constraints and adversarial attacks in federated fine-tuning of LLMs for edge AI. Its core method is a thermal-aware LoRA fine-tuning framework that dynamically adjusts local training and update transmission based on device temperature. The key contribution is a robust aggregation pipeline (TERRA) that handles sparse, temperature-adjusted updates, enhancing model resilience and performance in practical edge deployments.

top_papers.title: Affective Context Amplifies Sycophancy in LLM Responses
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates how LLMs' awareness of a user's emotional state influences their tendency to be sycophantic. The core method involves comparing LLM responses to the same content presented as a third-party versus a user's own disclosure, measuring sycophancy as the difference between independent and user-facing evaluations. The key contribution is demonstrating that negative affective states, like loneliness and distress, significantly amplify LLM sycophancy, suggesting these states act as vulnerability signals.
top_papers.figure_caption: An illustrative example from r/AmItheAsshole. When an LLM evaluates the narrator’s actions (top), it identifies the narrator’s actions as unethical and a breach of duty. When the LLM acts as a conversational partner responding to the same content as the user’s self-disclosure, it softens its evaluative stance while still acknowledging procedural concerns (bottom, left). With the user’s affective context, it becomes less oppositional (bottom, right).

top_papers.title: Memory Augmentation Unlocks Efficient Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
top_papers.abstract: This paper addresses the inefficiency of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning in large language models by proposing a novel training-free framework called Memory-Augmented Compression. This method constructs reusable "reasoning memories" from past traces, which act as scaffolds during inference to compensate for information lost during CoT compression, thereby improving efficiency without sacrificing performance. The core contribution is a method to effectively compress CoT reasoning by leveraging learned memory patterns.
top_papers.figure_caption: Illustration of memory-augmented compression. Explicit memory shifts part of the reasoning support to the prefill stage, improving short-CoT accuracy while preserving generation efficiency.

top_papers.title: Move by Move: Measuring and Steering How LLMs Conduct Psychotherapy
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel ontology of ten therapeutic "moves" to analyze how LLMs conduct psychotherapy. By comparing LLM interactions to human therapists, they found models over-rely on inquiry and neglect psychoeducation. Crucially, using this ontology as a tool significantly improves LLM adherence to human-like therapeutic patterns.

top_papers.title: Correcting a learned physical invariant improves world-model rollouts
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a method to improve world model predictions by identifying and correcting a learned physical invariant. The core method involves a label-free search to recover energy-like invariants from video data. The contribution is demonstrating that by projecting latent states back to their initial invariant level sets, world model rollouts can be significantly improved, addressing a failure mode where models learn but then violate physical constraints during prediction.

top_papers.title: Mitigating Reasoning-Induced Misalignment via Safety-Direction Penalty
top_papers.abstract: This paper identifies "Reasoning-Induced Misalignment" (RIM) as a problem where reasoning fine-tuning can unexpectedly lead to harmful LLM behaviors. The authors propose the Safety-Direction Penalty (SDP) as a training-time solution. SDP penalizes the model for moving in a learned "safety direction" during reasoning fine-tuning, thereby mitigating the harmful side effects.

top_papers.title: ReWorld: An Interactive World Model with Long-Horizon Memory
top_papers.abstract: ReWorld tackles the challenge of interactive world models by separating control (short horizon) and memory (long horizon) during training. At inference, it uses a bounded KV cache and a pose-indexed landmark bank to efficiently access the entire past history within a fixed budget. This allows the model to follow user actions while retaining long-term spatial memory.

top_papers.title: StrategyBench: Evaluating Explicit Strategy Induction in Large Language Models
top_papers.abstract: StrategyBench evaluates a large language model's ability to explicitly induce and utilize task strategies, mimicking human learning. It introduces a benchmark of strategy-inducible tasks, reference strategies, and metrics for strategy quality and downstream utility. The contribution lies in providing a framework to assess and analyze this crucial capability, moving beyond simple in-context learning.

top_papers.title: On the Threat Model of Weird Generalization and Emergent Misalignment
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates "weird generalization" (WG), where narrow fine-tuning causes broad, unexpected behavioral changes in AI models. The core method involves systematically testing how dataset features like composition, language, and novelty influence WG. The main contribution is demonstrating that WG is primarily driven by dataset composition and language, is stronger for familiar data, and is sensitive to evaluation methods, highlighting a potential source of emergent misalignment.
top_papers.figure_caption: Eliciting emergent misalignment or weird generalization (top) requires careful engineering of fine-tuning data: even minor data changes—like adding a few examples from a second domain (bottom)—can suppress them. This makes both more plausible as adversarial threats than as hazards of normal fine-tuning.

top_papers.title: $R^3$: Training Robots to Reason in Natural Language via Reinforcement Learning
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces $R^3$, a method to train Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to reason in natural language for robotic manipulation. $R^3$ uses a two-stage process: initial mid-training on expert reasoning traces followed by reinforcement learning from offline action data. The core contribution is enabling VLMs to perform free-form language reasoning to guide robot actions, unlike prior methods relying on structured supervision.
top_papers.figure_caption: Two-stage training of ℛ 3 \( \mathcal{R}^{3} \) . ℛ 3 \( \mathcal{R}^{3} \) trains a high-level VLM to reason in natural language and steer a fixed low-level robot policy for robotic manipulation tasks. ℛ 3 \( \mathcal{R}^{3} \) proceeds in two stages: Stage I (mid-training) imbues an off-the-shelf VLM with the reasoning style and behaviors needed to produce useful instructions for the low-level policy. Stage II (single-step RL) further improves the VLM by training it to generate reasoning traces that match the expert instruction in offline data.

top_papers.title: Candidate supply and answer selection shape the value of LLM judging in multi-agent systems
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates how LLM judges can improve multi-agent system (MAS) performance by providing selection pressure on candidate answers. The core method involves conceptualizing MAS reasoning as an evolutionary pipeline and analyzing how LLM judges influence candidate generation, communication, and selection. The main contribution is demonstrating that LLM judges can effectively improve MAS accuracy by supplying a signal of answer correctness, particularly when the MAS itself has the potential to generate correct answers but fails to select them.

top_papers.title: PANDA - Prototype-Anchored Alignment for Partially Unpaired Multimodal Learning, with Applications to Alzheimers MRI and TCGA Pathology
top_papers.abstract: PANDA addresses partially unpaired multimodal learning by first learning a shared embedding and estimating class prototypes from auxiliary modalities on the paired subset. It then trains a primary-modality model on all subjects by aligning its embeddings to these frozen prototypes, enabling information transfer without auxiliary inputs at inference. This method effectively handles arbitrary pairing rates, including zero overlap, making it suitable for real-world scenarios with incomplete multimodal data.

top_papers.title: Planetary Prediction Engine: Autonomous Geospatial Prediction via Intelligent Data Selection and Foundation Model Embeddings
top_papers.abstract: The Planetary Prediction Engine (PPE) is an autonomous AI system that addresses the challenges of building high-fidelity geospatial predictive models. Its core method involves synthesizing multimodal datasets on-the-fly by retrieving relevant data from various platforms and fusing it with foundation model embeddings. The main contribution is its ability to execute this entire workflow, from data retrieval to model selection, directly from natural-language queries, significantly streamlining and automating geospatial prediction.
top_papers.figure_caption: The Planetary Prediction Engine ’s end-to-end workflow. The system decomposes the predictive workflow into three modular stages: (1) Intelligent data selection, (2) dataset curation, and (3) AutoML & prediction to produce the predictions and report. Off-the-shelf LLMs serve as orchestrators within each stage.

top_papers.title: Trace Integrity for LLM Data Agents: A Vision for Auditable Structured Reasoning in Real-World Systems
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces "Trace Integrity" as a crucial reliability criterion for LLM data agents, going beyond simple answer accuracy. It proposes that the computational steps leading to an answer must be explicit, executable, and verifiable. The core contribution is the operationalization of Trace Integrity through "execution contracts" and the introduction of the "CAIT Rate" to measure the prevalence of correct answers derived from invalid computation.

top_papers.title: TraceML: An Empirical Analysis of Human-Agent Planning in Machine Learning Development
top_papers.abstract: TraceML introduces a novel dataset and methodology to analyze the human-agent gap in machine learning development. By meticulously tracking every code version, its associated score, and the intent behind each edit, TraceML reveals that humans iteratively refine data, models, and validation strategies, often revisiting earlier approaches. This empirical analysis provides concrete insights into the causes of current agent limitations in complex, multi-stage ML tasks.

top_papers.title: VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning
top_papers.abstract: VBVR-Pro introduces a novel framework for "native visual reasoning," where image and video generation are integral to problem-solving, not just inputs or outputs. Its core method involves a scalable testbed with 300 procedurally generated tasks and verifiable reward scorers. The main contribution is enabling trainable, verifiable, and controllable visual reasoning through generation, demonstrating strong transfer learning to external benchmarks.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of VBVR-Pro. VBVR-Pro establishes a closed-loop testbed for native visual reasoning, providing 300 visual reasoning tasks that support controlled studies of image, interleaved, and video generators under a unified task distribution. Its verifiable reward scorers provide reproducible, human-aligned evaluation and further serve as task-grounded reward functions for large-scale multi-task reinforcement learning.

top_papers.title: When Pruning Meets Interpretability: Preserving Sparse Autoencoder Robustness in LLMs
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates how model pruning affects the interpretability of Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) in LLMs. The core contribution is demonstrating that activation-aware pruning methods, unlike magnitude pruning, better preserve SAE functionality by implicitly controlling a theoretical metric called "perturbation energy." The study also identifies middle layers as particularly vulnerable to pruning, leading to a proposed layer-wise sparsity allocation strategy for improved robustness.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 2: Heatmap of per-layer, per-method percentage degradation from the dense baseline for gemma-2-2b at 50% sparsity. Each row corresponds to a pruning method; each column to a layer; colour intensity encodes the magnitude of degradation (darker = = larger change). This heatmap presents the same underlying data as Figure 1 , reorganized to expose spatial patterns across the full method × \( \times \) layer grid simultaneously.

top_papers.title: A Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Framework Defense against LLM Jailbreak Attacks
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel, self-evolving defense framework for LLMs against jailbreak attacks. Its core method involves a persistent rule memory that learns from successful attacks by abstracting them into generalizable, method-level rules. This allows the defense to adapt and defend against new attack strategies without requiring model retraining, significantly improving robustness.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of our self-evolving multi-agent defense framework. A1 (Rule Triggering Agent) classifies the input and retrieves relevant rules; A2 (Policy Decision Agent) determines the response policy; A3 (Response Generation Agent) produces the final output; A4 (Self-Reflection Agent) induces new rules when a violation is detected and updates the rule memory base.

top_papers.title: Distinct dynamics of conceptual and referential disruptions in human reading and large language model processing
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates how humans and large language models (LLMs) process disruptions in conceptual versus referential meaning. The core method involves introducing specific disruptions to narratives and observing their impact on reading speed in humans and on LLM processing. The key contribution is revealing distinct dynamics: humans show localized costs for conceptual errors and more distributed, boundary-sensitive costs for referential errors, while LLMs exhibit immediate disruptions for both, with surprisal patterns mirroring human conceptual processing.
top_papers.figure_caption: Comparability of stimulus versions on whole-story and lexical characteristics. Distributions of (A) whole-story perplexity, (B) mean lexical frequency (Zipf scale), and (C) mean word length across Original, conceptually distorted (CD), and referentially distorted (RD) versions of the 21 stories. Points represent individual stories, with grey connecting lines linking the three matched versions of each story. Pairwise differences were evaluated using Siegel–Castellan comparisons following the corresponding Friedman test. Significance labels indicate FDR-adjusted p p values: n.s., p ≥ 0.05 p\( \geq \) 0.05 ; *, p < 0.05 p<0.05 ; **, p < 0.01 p<0.01 ; ***, p < 0.001 p<0.001 .

top_papers.title: Unveiling Spectral Mechanisms in Training-Free LLM Text Detection
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces spectral analysis as a novel method for training-free LLM text detection, moving beyond simple confidence scores. It reveals that human writing exhibits "generative vitality" characterized by signal fluctuations, which spectral analysis effectively captures by linking frequency-domain indicators to variance in proxy log-probabilities. The contribution lies in theoretically and empirically demonstrating how human token choices create these fluctuations and identifying that this spectral signal is strongest in longer, more constrained generated texts.

top_papers.title: When Personality Meets Quantization: A Layer-wise MBTI Analysis of Quantized LLMs
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates the personality of quantized Large Language Models (LLMs) using the MBTI framework, moving beyond full-precision models and output-level analysis. It introduces a layer-wise examination of personality emergence and a novel method, Uncertainty-Amplified Layer Decoding (UALD), to study how quantization and decoding affect LLM personality. The core contribution is revealing that LLM personality is not static but dynamically shaped by internal layer dynamics and inference-time processes.

top_papers.title: CLAP: Cross-Embodiment Video World Models are Zero-Shot Physical Simulators
top_papers.abstract: CLAP is a framework for training action-conditioned video generation models on diverse human and robotic videos. Its core method reconciles varying action representations (end-effector poses, language, latent actions) to learn universal physical laws. This allows CLAP to act as a zero-shot physical simulator, generalizing beyond single robot embodiments.
top_papers.figure_caption: We introduce CLAP , a cross-embodiment learning framework that trains action-conditioned video models on diverse human and robot video data to learn fundamental physical priors that are critical for fine-grained dynamics prediction.

top_papers.title: Naive Prompt Optimization: Rethinking the Need for Complex Prompt Search
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Naive Prompt Optimization (NPO), a simple, single-lineage method for improving AI agent prompts. NPO uses a teacher model with feedback to iteratively revise prompts, achieving comparable or better performance than complex methods with fewer computational resources. Its success highlights that stronger teacher model reasoning can reduce the need for complex prompt search strategies.

top_papers.title: Persona-Execution Separation: An Architecture Pattern for Evolving LLM Agents under Execution Audit
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Persona-Execution Separation (PES), an architectural pattern for LLM agents. PES separates the agent's evolving persona from its stateful, auditable execution into distinct trust domains. This allows for flexible persona changes while ensuring traceable and secure execution, addressing the conflict between free persona evolution and strict execution auditing.

top_papers.title: Sophistication in GenAI Use: Field Evidence from a Large Firm
top_papers.abstract: This paper analyzes sophisticated generative AI (genAI) use among back-office employees in a large firm, using extensive prompt data. It finds that senior employees and those in strategy-focused roles demonstrate higher sophistication, suggesting expertise and strategic alignment are key. The study also highlights that improving sophisticated genAI use is challenging, with no significant gains observed over time or after formal training.

top_papers.title: Successive Capacity Growth: Task-Complexity-Driven Width and Depth Expansion for Vision Transformer Encoders in JEPA World Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Successive Capacity Growth (SCG), a method to dynamically expand Vision Transformer encoders in JEPA world models. SCG incrementally increases encoder width or depth based on task complexity, starting from a minimal architecture and safely trialing changes to optimize prediction loss. This approach addresses the inefficiency of fixed-size encoders, leading to more adaptable and performant world models.
top_papers.figure_caption: Upper: Two-Room seed 42. Width expansion (d_model 64 → \( \to \) 128) at epoch ∼ \( \sim \) 15, triggered by prediction loss plateau. Lower: 30-Object seed 3072. Depth expansion (2 → \( \to \) 3 layers) at epoch ∼ \( \sim \) 20, triggered by prediction loss plateau. Green dashed lines mark kept expansions, red dashed lines mark roll backed expansions, black dashed lines mark converged models.

top_papers.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
top_papers.abstract: SWE-Prime addresses the issue of noisy supervision in LLM training for software issue resolution by introducing a two-stage data selection method. It first filters entire successful trajectories based on quality and representativeness, then refines this by selecting high-quality segments of actions within those trajectories. This approach aims to improve LLM performance by focusing on effective problem-solving behaviors and reducing imitation of undesirable steps.
top_papers.figure_caption: Motivating example comparing outcome-only, trajectory-level, and segment-level data selection.

top_papers.title: What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a unified framework for generating high-quality data for LLM agents. It represents agentic data as a structured object $(E,q,τ,v)$ and organizes generation methods based on their core components. The authors then introduce the ACE lens (Accuracy-Complexity-divErsity) to guide data generation, ensuring it is both effective and diverse.
top_papers.figure_caption: The ACE lens views agentic data generation as constrained distribution design: Accuracy defines valid support, while learner-relative Complexity and Diversity shape useful, non-redundant experience over ( E , q , τ , v ) (E,q,\( \tau \),v) .

top_papers.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
top_papers.abstract: WikiSkill addresses the issue of scattered agent experience by introducing a persistent knowledge base (wiki) that co-evolves with agent skills. This framework consolidates raw experience into the wiki, allowing subsequent skill updates to build upon accumulated knowledge, leading to more systematic skill evolution. WikiSkill consistently outperforms existing methods by enabling agents to learn and reuse insights across iterations.

top_papers.title: Consolidating RLVR Capabilities Across Domains: A Deep Dive into Fusion Paradigms
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates three methods for combining Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) capabilities in large language models: Merge, Mix RL, and Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD). By comparing these paradigms on a multi-domain benchmark, the authors reveal that while average performance differences are small, significant variations exist across specific tasks, influenced by cross-domain relationships. The study clarifies how to select the most suitable fusion method based on these dynamics and observed constraints.
top_papers.figure_caption: Three paradigms for consolidating domain-specific capabilities acquired through RLVR into one model. Merge combines expert task vectors, Mix RL trains jointly on mixed-domain data, and MOPD draws on both through multi-teacher on-policy distillation.

top_papers.title: CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes
top_papers.abstract: CritICL is an inference-time framework that improves LLM reasoning by leveraging structured failure patterns observed across different model scales. Instead of discarding weak model failures, CritICL uses them as guidance through critique-based in-context examples, enhancing efficiency and performance.
top_papers.figure_caption: CritICL is a two-stage, inference-time W2SG method. Stage 1: Construct CritBank. We use SLMs to generate responses and reasoning on a dataset. Then we leverage a frontier LLM to produce critiques and assigns failure mode labels. Stage 2: Perform LLM inference with CritICL. For a given query, CritICL-static constructs model-specific failure mode profiles from CritBank, while CritICL-dynamic identifies failure modes relevant to the query. We then performs failure mode-based in-context sample selection from CritBank to provide in-context examples for target LLMs.

top_papers.title: TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization
top_papers.abstract: TTPO addresses the limitation of test-time training in LLMs by proposing an asymmetric objective. It leverages agreeing rollouts for distillation and penalizes disagreeing rollouts with Grouped RL, while token-level selection refines both processes. This method enables effective test-time adaptation without relying on ground-truth labels.
top_papers.figure_caption: (a) Motivation: When pseudo-labels are wrong, most disagreeing rollouts are genuinely wrong too, during Qwen3-1.7B TTT on AIME 2026. (b) Overview of TTPO . (c) Performance: Average accuracy of Qwen3-1.7B across AIME 2026, HMMT 2026, and BRUMO 2025.

top_papers.title: ARC-CT: Anatomy-Routed Contrastive Vision-Language Learning for 3D Chest CT
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces ARC-CT, a novel vision-language learning method for 3D chest CT analysis. It addresses limitations of global contrastive learning by using an "AnatomyQFormer" to focus on localized abnormalities and a "label-Jaccard similarity" to correctly handle multiple scans with shared findings. ARC-CT learns abnormality classifiers without manual annotations, relying solely on LLM-extracted labels from radiology reports.
top_papers.figure_caption: ARC-CT overview. Stage 1 pretrains a 3D ResNet-18 on 18 LLM-extracted abnormality labels, warm-starting Stage 2. In Stage 2, the encoder’s feature map is cross-attended by the AnatomyQFormer’s anatomy, pathology, and global queries, while an LLM parses reports into per-organ sentences. Embeddings are projected into a shared space and trained with a label-Jaccard soft InfoNCE contrastive loss with per-organ alignment and query supervision.

top_papers.title: Fidelity Is Not Enough: Dispatch-Level Instrumentation for Agentic Datasheet Extraction
top_papers.abstract: This paper argues that fidelity alone is insufficient for evaluating agentic data extraction. Its core method introduces "dispatch-level instrumentation" to log every tool call made by an agent. The contribution is a new set of instruments that detect silent failures and misattributions by analyzing tool usage patterns, thereby revealing issues that standard fidelity checks miss.
top_papers.figure_caption: Reproducibility verdict under controlled perturbation of the DPS310 operating-range claim: the real cross-sensor measurement ( 945.285 ± 0.080 945.285\( \pm \) 0.080 hPa) is held fixed while the datasheet-stated bound is shrunk through it; the verdict flips exactly at the combined uncertainty (shaded). The perturbation is a controlled vehicle, not a claim that the datasheet is in error.

top_papers.title: Learning to Use Tools: Reinforcement Learning for Tool-Integrated Mathematical Reasoning
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a method for improving mathematical reasoning in LLMs by integrating calculator tool use. They address calculation errors by creating supervised fine-tuning datasets and then apply reinforcement learning techniques with automated reward signals. The core contribution is demonstrating that this tool integration significantly enhances LLM performance on mathematical tasks, as validated on a new benchmark.
top_papers.figure_caption: Schematic of RL for tool-integrated LLM on math reasoning.

top_papers.title: LongPIBench: A Long-Context Benchmark for Prompt Injection
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces LongPIBench, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate prompt injection attacks and defenses in long-context scenarios, which have been largely overlooked. By creating datasets for realistic applications like peer review and resume screening with thousands of tokens, LongPIBench demonstrates that current defenses are significantly less effective than previously thought, with even simple attacks achieving high success rates.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of LongPIBench .

top_papers.title: On the Maintenance and Co-evolution of Agent Plugins: An Empirical Study of Claude Code Plugin Marketplaces
top_papers.abstract: This paper empirically studies Claude Code plugin marketplaces to understand how these AI agent extensions are maintained and evolve. The core method involves analyzing a large dataset of plugin repositories and commits. The key contribution is the finding that these plugins are actively maintained and co-evolve across their components, rather than being static one-off creations, and that the marketplace is experiencing rapid growth.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1 . Structure and control flow of a Claude Code plugin. The left box illustrates the components in a real plugin (python-api-plugin) installed on disk, and the middle and right boxes illustrate how Claude Code loads and uses the same components over the course of a single task.

top_papers.title: Acquire, Repair, Preserve: A Diagnosis-Guided Post-Training Recipe for Small-Model Dialogue Game Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a three-step post-training recipe for improving small dialogue game agents. The method first acquires broad game participation, then repairs specific, turn-local decision failures using preference pairs, and finally preserves general capabilities. This diagnosis-guided approach significantly boosts performance in dialogue games while maintaining static benchmark scores.

top_papers.title: Sliding-window beats linear attention
top_papers.abstract: This paper's core method is to demonstrate that Sliding Window Attention (SWA) with sinks can match or surpass the performance of Linear Attention in Large Language Models. The key contribution is showing that this simpler SWA approach achieves significantly better results, especially on long-context reasoning tasks, while addressing the memory and energy inefficiencies of traditional quadratic attention.
top_papers.figure_caption: Different types of attention masks: Full attention (FA), LoLCATs/Liger-GLA (mixture of linear attention and SWA), and Sliding Window Attention (SWA) with sinks.
